answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each claimed agent to a Wesolowski VDF requiring a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before a proof is accepted. Since every squaring depends on the preceding result, an attacker cannot split one identity’s work across GPUs; simulating many clones therefore multiplies the required sequential effort and wall-clock delay, establishing a physical Sybil bottleneck. Cedar, nadir, and yarrow serve only as challenge inputs, not computational shortcuts.
